frequency_question: How often do executive principals with the stated intent and formal capability to revoke the recognized status of a major accrediting or regulatory proxy actually follow through and execute the final revocation within a comparable timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes instances where a federal department or cabinet-level agency initiated and completed a formal review resulting in the total termination of a recognized accrediting agency or delegated standard-setting body's authority. Excludes mere threats, voluntary relinquishments, or partial suspensions that do not reach final revocation.

cases.name: Department of Education de-recognition of the American College of Midwifery and Obstetrics (1991)
Department of Education withdrawal of recognition from the Association of Independent Colleges and Schools (AICS) (1993)
Department of Education termination of recognition for the Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) (2016 / reaffirmed 2018)
Department of Education final termination of ACICS recognition (second cycle) (2022)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named major historical full de-recognition events of institutional/programmatic accreditors by the US Department of Education.
known_gaps: Excludes minor specialty accreditors that surrendered status voluntarily rather than facing an enforced departmental revocation order.
skeleton: Recognized accrediting agencies facing formal departmental pressure for total de-recognition where the executive principal exercises absolute authority to terminate status.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 documented major full-revocation proceedings initiated with intent by executive principals against national accreditors over the period.
validity_reason: The base rate reflects historical Department of Education administrative follow-through on accreditor recognition, which remains stable across presidential administrations when agency leadership exhibits explicit intent.
